Hi Tom — appreciate the questions. Below are authoritative answers you can share with legal/infra. I’ve kept each point concise and included the operational controls we rely on. See attached Redwood-DPA-Summary.pdf for contract language excerpts; full DPA is available via the DocuSign link when you’re ready.

1) Region pinning and data locality:
- Dedicated deployments can be pinned to a single cloud region (e.g., us-west-2).
- All customer inference traffic, model KV cache, and stored artifacts for your tenant are provisioned into isolated VPC subnets within that region.
- Our control plane maintains metadata for management but customer payloads and tokens are routed to the pinned region for inference execution. We do not send inference request payloads outside the pinned region for processing.

2) Retention windows & on-demand deletion:
- Transient KV caches: default TTL is 72 hours; cache behavior is configurable and can be set to 0 for no persistent caching if required.
- Request logs (short-term operational logs used for debugging): retained for 7 days by default; retention can be shortened to 0 upon request for Dedicated customers under an agreed configuration profile.
- Long-term audit logs (for compliance) are retained per the DPA; retention duration is configurable in the Dedicated contract.
- On-demand deletion: we support a tenant-scoped deletion workflow. When you request deletion, we execute: 1) clear KV caches in runtime nodes, 2) purge request logs and ephemeral storage, 3) mark data for deletion in backup inventories and initiate deletion there (see backups section). We provide an attestation once the workflow completes.

3) Backups & replication:
- Default snapshot/backup policy is region-local for Dedicated customers. We do not replicate backups to a secondary region unless replication is explicitly enabled in the customer contract for disaster recovery.
- If you require no cross-region replication, we will disable any automated replication for your tenant.

4) Deletion attestation and verification:
- We provide a standardized deletion attestation that includes: timestamp, objects deleted (by key namespace), and nodes involved.
- For additional assurance, we can produce secure hashes and counters from deletion runs and time-stamped log excerpts (redacted for other tenants) as part of the attestation.

Operational notes and constraints:
- Encryption: data at rest is encrypted with tenant-specific keys (KMS) and in transit with TLS. You may bring your own KMS keys for Dedicated (BYOK) to satisfy stricter key residency requirements.
- Support for air-gapped/on-prem: for highly regulated workflows we offer Private (on-prem) deployments where the control plane can be configured to limit metadata exchange; this is a separate engagement.
- SLAs & evidence: SOC2 Type II report is attached; specific SLA clauses for deletion timelines and region pinning appear in the DPA.

Attachments: Redwood-DPA-Summary.pdf (contract excerpts); we will provide the full DPA via DocuSign when you confirm the account-level contacts.

If you want a single-page attestation template we can issue immediately after you sign the DPA; otherwise we can run a pre-procurement demo showing the tenant pinned to us-west-2.

Hi Tom — quick formal confirmations for your procurement packet below. You have permission to include these statements with the DPA excerpts attached (Redwood-DPA-Summary.pdf).

1) Backups and replication: "For the Dedicated tenant provisioned for Alpha Health (DEAL-4831), automated backups and snapshots are configured as region-local (us-west-2). Cross-region replication is not enabled for this tenant and will not be enabled without explicit written authorization from Alpha Health."

2) Audit/log artifacts after deletion: "Redwood does not persist re-identifiable customer payloads in any analytics pipelines following an agreed deletion event. Operational audit logs that are necessary for internal diagnostics may contain redacted metadata only; PII or inference payloads are purged as part of the deletion workflow described in the DPA. If Alpha Health requires cryptographic proof of deletion for specific namespaces, Redwood will provide hash-based verification as part of the deletion attestation."

3) Attestation turnaround: standard attestation turnaround is 5 business days from the formal deletion request receipt. Expedited attestation (2 business days) can be offered under an SOW amendment.
